summary: The case involves a testamentary disposition under a Will dated 15.4.1968 by Tulsi Ram, who bequeathed property to his son (the appellant, Jogi Ram) with absolute rights and to his second wife, Ram Devi, with a limited life interest, prohibiting alienation. After decades of litigation, the appellant challenged sale deeds executed by Ram Devi during her life, which were initially set aside by a 1995 decree confirming her limited interest under Section 14(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956. The High Court in 2018 reversed, holding that Ram Devi’s limited interest had crystallized into absolute ownership under Section 14(1) as a pre-existing right, relying on V. Tulasamma and Jupudy Pardha Sarathy. It also held res judicata did not apply due to a change in law and that no substantial question of law was required under the Punjab Courts Act. The Supreme Court considered these determinations in appeal.
